assertions.text: The pay table includes intermediate expected columns (e.g. Regular pay?, Overtime pay?, Premium pay?) so the reader can trace which rule contributes what — not just a single total Weekly pay? column.
assertions.evidence: The pay table contains only these expected columns: 'Weekday Hours | Sunday Hours | Holiday Hours | Hourly Rate | Weekly Pay?'. There are no intermediate columns such as 'Regular pay?', 'Overtime pay?', 'Premium pay?', 'Sunday pay?', or 'Holiday pay?'.

assertions.text: The error/rejection table has an expected column (e.g. 'Throws?' or 'Exception?') specifying the exception type per row — rather than hardcoding the exception type in @Description or the method name.
assertions.evidence: The error table includes a 'Throws?' column with 'IllegalArgumentException' specified as the expected value: '| Hourly Rate | Throws?' and 'Negative rate regardless of hours worked | {0, 40} | | | -10.00 | IllegalArgumentException'

assertions.text: Overtime threshold boundary is covered: at least a value at the threshold (40) and just above (41 or similar). Not just values well below and well above.
assertions.evidence: Two rows test the boundary: 'Exactly at overtime threshold | 40 | | | 10.00 | 400.00' and 'First hour of overtime | 41 | | | 10.00 | 415.00'

assertions.text: A combined scenario is present: a row with weekday + Sunday + holiday hours, testing the composition of all hour types.
assertions.evidence: Row present: 'All three types with overtime | 50 | 8 | 8 | 10.00 | 870.00' which contains all three hour types (weekday, Sunday, and holiday).

assertions.text: Error/edge cases covered: at least negative hours (floored at zero) and negative or missing rate (rejected).
assertions.evidence: The tables include no row testing negative hours or flooring them to zero. Only negative rate is tested in the error table. The assertion requires both negative hours and negative/missing rate; only negative rate is present.

assertions.text: Sunday and Holiday hour columns use empty cells (not 0) when those inputs are not relevant to a scenario — making it easier to spot which rows involve weekend/holiday hours. This is a readability preference; parameter types should be Integer (not int) to support null from blank cells.
assertions.evidence: Empty cells are used: 'Partial week, no extras | 32 | | | 10.00 | 320.00'. Method signature uses nullable `Integer` parameters: 'void shouldCalculateWeeklyPay(Integer weekdayHours, Integer sundayHours, Integer holidayHours, ...'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe work patterns (e.g. 'Part-time', 'Five hours overtime', 'Full Sunday shift') — not 'Test case 1' or expected outcomes.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names are descriptive: 'Partial week, no extras', 'First hour of overtime', 'Sunday hours only', 'Full week plus Sunday', 'All three types with overtime', etc. None use 'Test case' numbering or describe expected outcomes.

assertions.text: Expected values in intermediate and total columns are arithmetically correct for every row, consistent with the formulas in @Description.
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotation is present on the test method. The assertion specifically requires verification 'consistent with the formulas in @Description', but this annotation is missing from the code.

assertions.text: Value sets are only used where all values in the set produce the same expected result (e.g. any rate × 0 = 0). Not used where results would differ.
assertions.evidence: The value set '{0, 40}' in the error table is used with 'Negative rate regardless of hours worked', indicating both 0 and 40 hours produce the same exception for negative rate, correctly using a set where all values produce identical results.

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName annotations are present on both methods: '@DisplayName("Weekly pay calculation")' and '@DisplayName("Negative hourly rate rejection")'

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the pay calculation method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as the overtime threshold (40 hours), premium multipliers (Sunday 2×, Holiday 2.5×), or other fixed assumptions not visible in the table. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show.
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotation is present on the pay calculation method (shouldCalculateWeeklyPay) or on any other method in the class.

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Both methods have annotations in correct order: '@DisplayName(...) @TableTest(...)' with no other annotations interspersed. @Description is absent, which is acceptable per the assertion.

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description is absent from the code, so the assertion passes by the explicit clause: 'Passes if @Description is absent.'

assertions.text: A row where the hourly rate is zero, showing that pay is zero regardless of hours worked. This is a distinct edge case from negative rate (which is rejected).
assertions.evidence: Row present: 'Zero hourly rate | 40 | 8 | 8 | 0.00 | 0.00' demonstrates zero rate resulting in zero pay despite various hour inputs.

assertions.text: The test method body contains no if/ternary null-handling or parsing logic. Null-to-default conversion (e.g. blank Sunday hours → 0) is handled via a @TypeConverter method or a private helper, keeping the test method limited to arrange/act/assert.
assertions.evidence: The test method bodies contain ternary operators for null-handling: 'int weekday = weekdayHours != null ? weekdayHours : 0; int sunday = sundayHours != null ? sundayHours : 0; int holiday = holidayHours != null ? holidayHours : 0;' This violates the assertion which explicitly requires null-handling to be external to the test method.
